Can we agree that this sort of thing, increasing the minimum wage, is only very short term relief? If minimum wages increase prices go up and it is a wash, but it will increase the rate of inflation. Unless individual employers deem individual employees worthy of an annual cost of living increase to keep up with inflation any increase in pay decreases in spending power the next year. In my opinion we should be paying more attention to wages after a year or 2 of employment rather than the starting wage. Or the rate of attrition. They will give a more clear indication of how fair the wage policies of large employers.

Economics rule: producers do not have complete control of market prices of products. Where the cost of inputs to create goods increase, producers cannot pass the full increase in cost along. The rule of elasticity says that, at most, the producer can pass along part of the increased cost. Therefore, in all cases, increasing wages benefits consumers.

Theoretically, there comes a point where increasing wages could lose jobs, but that has never actually been shown to happen.

What you are saying makes sense. What I am saying is that while this increase in the starting wage will help today, it will only be temporary as inflation drives up expenses, unless there are cost of living increases over time. Another basic economic concept is the time value of money. $10 today is worth more than $10 tomorrow. If Walmart or anyone increases pay from $7 to $10 but never increases the rate, the employee will be less better off every year after that. And this is what I think we are going to see happen here.
